words.enDefinition: A coordinated programme of public relations work with a defined purpose, audience, and period or set of activities.

examples.en: The fictional museum runs a PR campaign to explain new opening hours before the semester begins.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆开展一项「公关活动」，在学期开始之前说明新的开放时间。

examples.en: Our seminar separates the PR campaign from the one announcement used to introduce the library programme.
examples.zh: 研讨课把整项「公关活动」与介绍图书馆项目的那份公告区分开。

words.enDefinition: Communication by an organisation with members of the public about its activities, decisions, or services.

examples.en: The casebook introduces public communications through a fictional college sharing information about changes to community access.
examples.zh: 案例教材以虚构大学公布社区使用权限变化为例，介绍「公众沟通」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which documents count as public communications when the fictional university closes a study space.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构大学关闭一处自习空间时，哪些文件属于「公众沟通」。

words.enDefinition: An organisational function that coordinates communication with internal and external groups on behalf of a company.

examples.en: The sample organisation chart places corporate communications alongside several teams in a fictitious book distribution company.
examples.zh: 样本组织结构图把「企业传播」与一家虚构图书批发企业中的其他团队并列展示。

examples.en: Our seminar discusses corporate communications when comparing the company's staff bulletin with its public service announcement.
examples.zh: 研讨课对照公司内部员工简报和公开服务公告，讨论「企业传播」。

words.enDefinition: An organisation's communication with people and groups outside the organisation, including partners, media, and the public.

examples.en: The fictional college puts the notice for neighbouring residents under external communications in its sample plan.
examples.zh: 虚构大学在示例计划里，将发给附近居民的通知归入「对外沟通」。

examples.en: Our class separates external communications about the exhibition from emails sent only to the organising team.
examples.zh: 全班把关于展览的「对外沟通」与只发给组织团队的邮件分开。

words.enDefinition: Communication intended for an organisation's members or employees about its work, plans, or decisions.

examples.en: The sample plan describes internal communications for staff who will answer questions about the revised opening hours.
examples.zh: 样本计划说明了面向将回答新开放时间问题的工作人员的「内部沟通」。

examples.en: Our exercise asks which items belong under internal communications in a fictional college library's planning document.
examples.zh: 练习询问，虚构大学图书馆的计划文件中哪些事项属于「内部沟通」。

words.enDefinition: A specified change or result that a communication effort is intended to achieve for an audience.

examples.en: The fictional plan states a communications objective of improving understanding of the library's revised opening hours.
examples.zh: 虚构计划写明一项「传播目标」，即让读者更清楚图书馆调整后的开放时间。

examples.en: Our tutor asks how the communications objective differs from the activities listed in the fictional plan.
examples.zh: 老师询问，这项「传播目标」与虚构计划列出的活动有何不同。

collocations: measure progress towards a communications objective

words.enDefinition: An overall approach specifying how communication is intended to support organisational goals and audience needs.

examples.en: The fictional recreation centre's communications strategy explains how residents will learn about new booking arrangements.
examples.zh: 虚构活动中心的「传播策略」解释了居民将如何获知新的预约安排。

examples.en: Our class assesses whether the communications strategy addresses the concerns listed in the sample public feedback report.
examples.zh: 全班评估「传播策略」是否回应了公众反馈报告样本中列出的关切。

words.enDefinition: A working document that sets out communication activities, responsibilities, timing, and evaluation for specified objectives.

examples.en: The fictional university's communications plan lists who will publish each notice about the replacement study space.
examples.zh: 虚构大学的「传播计划」列明关于替代自习空间的各项通知将由谁发布。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the communications plan includes a timetable for answering public questions about the change.
examples.zh: 全班核对「传播计划」是否包含回答公众对该变化所提问题的时间表。

words.enDefinition: A systematic review of how an organisation currently communicates, including its channels, materials, or their effectiveness.

examples.en: The sample communications audit compares notices from different departments about the same fictional programme for residents.
examples.zh: 「传播工作审查」样本对比了不同部门就同一项虚构居民项目发布的通知。

examples.en: Our seminar asks which kinds of evidence the communications audit uses to assess the fictional organisation's materials.
examples.zh: 研讨课询问，「传播工作审查」依据哪些证据评估虚构机构的传播材料。

words.enDefinition: The person responsible for coordinating communication for a particular project, team, or situation.

examples.en: The fictional planning chart identifies the communications lead responsible for keeping departments informed about the schedule.
examples.zh: 虚构计划表列明负责向各部门通报日程的「传播工作负责人」。

examples.en: Our exercise asks the communications lead in the fictional team to check which office owns each announcement.
examples.zh: 练习中，虚构团队的「传播工作负责人」要核对每项公告由哪个部门发布。

collocations: assign a communications lead to a project

words.enDefinition: An external firm providing public relations planning, media work, or related communication services to clients.

examples.en: The casebook describes a PR agency hired to support the fictional gallery's public opening programme for residents.
examples.zh: 案例教材描述了一家受雇协助虚构画廊开展居民开放项目的「公关代理机构」。

examples.en: Our class compares the PR agency's proposed role with the work the fictional gallery keeps in house.
examples.zh: 全班将「公关代理机构」拟承担的工作与虚构画廊留在机构内部处理的工作作比较。

words.enDefinition: A group employed within an organisation to perform its public relations work.

examples.en: The fictional university's in-house PR team coordinates the outreach materials for a public library exhibition on campus.
examples.zh: 虚构大学的「内部公关团队」统筹校园图书馆公开展览的宣传材料。

examples.en: Our case compares the work of an in-house PR team with tasks assigned to an outside agency.
examples.zh: 案例比较了「内部公关团队」的工作与交给外部代理机构的任务。

collocations: work of an in-house PR team

words.enDefinition: An organisational unit that handles enquiries from journalists and coordinates media communication.

examples.en: The fictional college directs reporters to its press office for questions about the new reading room's opening.
examples.zh: 虚构大学请记者向其「新闻联络办公室」咨询新阅览室的开放事宜。

examples.en: Our sample website places the press office address beside the section containing official announcements and media contacts.
examples.zh: 样本网站把「新闻联络办公室」地址放在收录正式公告和媒体联络人的栏目旁。

words.enDefinition: A staff member responsible for dealing with journalists and coordinating an organisation's press enquiries or statements.

examples.en: The fictional press officer checks which department can answer a reporter's question about the revised museum opening.
examples.zh: 虚构的「新闻联络专员」核对哪个部门能回答记者关于博物馆新开放时间的问题。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks who acts as press officer at the fictional institution when the usual contact is absent.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，在常用联系人缺席时，虚构机构由谁担任「新闻联络专员」。

words.enDefinition: An official responsible for providing accurate information to the public and media on behalf of an organisation or agency.

examples.en: The casebook lists the public information officer as the contact for questions about a fictional community centre closure.
examples.zh: 案例教材把「公众信息专员」列为虚构社区中心关闭问题的联系人。

examples.en: Our class compares the responsibilities of a public information officer with those of the staff preparing internal reports.
examples.zh: 全班把「公众信息专员」的职责与负责编写内部报告的员工职责作比较。

collocations: public information officer for an agency

words.enDefinition: A senior officer responsible for an organisation's overall communication work or policy.

examples.en: The fictional college's communications director approves the scope of a project for sharing information with local residents.
examples.zh: 虚构大学的「传播事务总监」批准了向当地居民公布信息的项目范围。

examples.en: Our organisation chart places the communications director above several teams handling different kinds of public information.
examples.zh: 组织结构图将「传播事务总监」置于几个分别处理不同类型公众信息的团队之上。

words.enDefinition: A person formally chosen to speak on a particular topic or on behalf of an organisation.

examples.en: The announcement identifies a designated spokesperson for the fictional college's questions about changes to campus access.
examples.zh: 公告为虚构大学有关校园出入变动的问题指明了一位「指定发言人」。

examples.en: Our worksheet explains why the designated spokesperson handles requests for an official comment in the fictional example.
examples.zh: 练习单解释，在虚构示例中为何由「指定发言人」处理正式置评请求。

words.enDefinition: An information session or document preparing a spokesperson with relevant, verified facts and context before speaking.

examples.en: The fictional spokesperson briefing lists the revised dates and the department responsible for each part of the project.
examples.zh: 虚构「发言人情况简报」列出了调整后的日期，以及项目各环节的负责部门。

examples.en: Our case asks which facts should appear in the spokesperson briefing before the fictional media session begins.
examples.zh: 案例询问，虚构媒体活动开始以前应在「发言人情况简报」中列明哪些事实。

words.enDefinition: Communication with groups or people who affect or are affected by an organisation's activities or decisions.

examples.en: The sample plan covers stakeholder communications with staff, local residents, and groups that use the fictional venue.
examples.zh: 样本计划涵盖与虚构场地的工作人员、当地居民及使用团体的「利益相关方沟通」。

examples.en: Our class discusses stakeholder communications when reviewing who needs information about the fictional library's shortened hours.
examples.zh: 全班回顾哪些人需要了解虚构图书馆缩短开放时间的信息，并讨论「利益相关方沟通」。

words.enDefinition: A process of involving affected or interested groups through activities such as consultation, dialogue, or partnership.

examples.en: The fictional college includes stakeholder engagement so library users can comment on options for the temporary space.
examples.zh: 虚构大学安排「利益相关方参与」，让图书馆使用者可以就临时场地的选项发表意见。

examples.en: Our casebook distinguishes stakeholder engagement from announcements that only tell people which option was selected in the example.
examples.zh: 案例教材把「利益相关方参与」与示例中只告知选定哪一方案的公告区分开。

words.enDefinition: An organisation's work to develop and maintain constructive relationships with the communities affected by its activities.

examples.en: The sample report describes community relations through a fictional museum's ongoing dialogue with residents around the site.
examples.zh: 样本报告通过虚构博物馆与周边居民的持续对话，描述「社区关系」工作。

examples.en: Our class discusses community relations using examples of joint events between a fictional college and nearby groups.
examples.zh: 课堂用虚构大学与附近团体合办活动的例子讨论「社区关系」。

words.enDefinition: Work involving an organisation's relationships and communication with public institutions and groups concerned with public policy.

examples.en: The course introduces public affairs through a fictional university discussing library access with a local council.
examples.zh: 课程用虚构大学与地方议会讨论图书馆开放范围的例子介绍「公共事务沟通」。

examples.en: Our casebook distinguishes public affairs from advertising an event to prospective visitors in the same fictional project.
examples.zh: 案例教材将「公共事务沟通」与同一虚构项目中向潜在访客宣传活动区分开来。

words.enDefinition: A person designated to maintain communication between an organisation and local residents or groups.

examples.en: The fictional museum names a community liaison officer for residents with questions about the building work nearby.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆指定一名「社区联络专员」，供对附近施工有疑问的居民联系。

examples.en: Our exercise asks how the community liaison officer reports recurring questions to the staff responsible for the project.
examples.zh: 练习询问，「社区联络专员」怎样向项目负责人反映反复出现的问题。

collocations: responsibilities of a community liaison officer

words.enDefinition: Independent attention or coverage an organisation receives through external media without buying or controlling the placement.

examples.en: The fictional project records earned media when a local newspaper independently reports on its new reading programme.
examples.zh: 当地报纸独立报道虚构项目的新阅读计划，项目记录这项报道为「免费媒体报道」。

examples.en: Our worksheet classifies the newspaper article as earned media because the outlet made its own editorial decision.
examples.zh: 练习单将该报刊文章归为「免费媒体报道」，因为媒体自行作出了编辑决定。

words.enDefinition: In the PESO model, communication shared or co-created by organisations and audiences on social platforms or similar networks.

examples.en: The classroom example illustrates shared media through a fictional community group's voluntary repost of a university announcement.
examples.zh: 课堂示例借虚构社区团体自愿转发大学公告的一幕说明「社交共创传播」。

examples.en: The team credited shared media when local readers discussed and recirculated the library's opening announcement.
examples.zh: 本地读者讨论并转发图书馆开放公告时，团队把这种传播视为「社交共创传播」。

words.enDefinition: A communication framework grouping channels or activities as paid, earned, shared, and owned media.

examples.en: The seminar introduces the PESO model by classifying several fictional examples of work for a university exhibition.
examples.zh: 研讨课对大学展览的几个虚构传播案例作分类，以介绍「PESO传播渠道模型」。

examples.en: Our worksheet uses the PESO model to distinguish independent news coverage from notices published by the museum itself.
examples.zh: 练习单用「PESO传播渠道模型」区分独立新闻报道与博物馆自行发布的通知。

words.enDefinition: Coordinated communication intended to give the public practical information about an issue, change, or service.

examples.en: The fictional library runs a public information campaign explaining how readers can use its temporary study space.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆开展「公众信息传播活动」，说明读者怎样使用临时自习空间。

examples.en: Our casebook connects the public information campaign to the practical questions residents asked in the sample feedback.
examples.zh: 案例教材把「公众信息传播活动」与居民在反馈样本里提出的实际问题联系起来。

words.enDefinition: A coordinated effort intended to make a defined audience more aware of an issue, organisation, or service.

examples.en: The fictional public awareness campaign tells residents that the university library offers a public reading area on weekends.
examples.zh: 虚构「公众认知宣传活动」告诉居民，大学图书馆周末设有公众阅览区。

examples.en: Our class assesses the public awareness campaign by comparing synthetic awareness measures from before and after the project.
examples.zh: 全班通过比较项目前后的合成认知度指标来评估「公众认知宣传活动」。

collocations: objective of a public awareness campaign

words.enDefinition: A schedule showing when planned communication activities or materials are due across a project or organisation.

examples.en: The fictional communications calendar lists the dates for community notices and a staff briefing about the exhibition.
examples.zh: 虚构「传播事项日历」列出展览社区通知及工作人员说明会的日期。

examples.en: Our class checks the communications calendar to see whether both scheduled releases concern the same announcement.
examples.zh: 全班查看「传播事项日历」，核对两次计划发布是否涉及同一公告。

words.enDefinition: A structure organising the key ideas, supporting points, and audience considerations of communication on a topic.

examples.en: The sample messaging framework groups the fictional library's main points with the details supporting each one.
examples.zh: 「传播信息框架」样本把虚构图书馆的主要要点及其各自的支撑细节归在一起。

examples.en: Our exercise uses the messaging framework to identify why the internal briefing and public notice cover similar facts.
examples.zh: 练习用「传播信息框架」说明为什么内部说明会和公众通知都涵盖相似的事实。

words.enDefinition: A visual framework shaped like a house, with an overarching message supported by pillars and evidence.

examples.en: The course handout illustrates a message house using the fictional museum's central idea and three supporting points.
examples.zh: 课程讲义借虚构博物馆的一项中心观点和三项支撑要点，说明「房屋式信息框架」。

examples.en: Our group identified which facts supported the pillars in the message house printed in the sample communication plan.
examples.zh: 小组辨认哪些事实支撑样本传播计划中「房屋式信息框架」的各根支柱。

words.enDefinition: A central point an organisation wants an audience to understand or remember about a topic.

examples.en: The fictional library's key message states that the alternative study room remains available during building repairs.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆的「核心传播信息」指出，建筑维修期间替代自习室仍可使用。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which supporting details explain the key message in the notice for the fictional community centre.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，哪些补充细节解释了虚构社区中心通知里的「核心传播信息」。

words.enDefinition: Agreement of central facts and points across communications while allowing wording or presentation to vary.

examples.en: The fictional team checks message consistency by comparing the dates given in a briefing and a public notice.
examples.zh: 虚构团队对照说明会和公众通知给出的日期，检查「传播口径一致性」。

examples.en: Our class finds message consistency in two announcements that use different wording but give the same opening hours.
examples.zh: 全班在两份措辞不同、却给出相同开放时间的公告中看到了「传播口径一致性」。

words.enDefinition: The part of public relations concerned with ongoing communication between an organisation and news media.

examples.en: The seminar introduces media relations through a fictional museum answering local reporters' questions about an exhibition.
examples.zh: 研讨课用虚构博物馆回答当地记者关于展览的问题，介绍「媒体关系」。

examples.en: Our casebook treats media relations as ongoing work, including responding to enquiries after the event has ended.
examples.zh: 案例教材把「媒体关系」视为持续性工作，包括在活动结束后回应咨询。

words.enDefinition: A request from a journalist or media outlet for information, comment, or an interview.

examples.en: The fictional press office receives a media inquiry about the dates of the university's public reading exhibition.
examples.zh: 虚构新闻联络办公室收到一项关于大学公开阅读展览日期的「媒体问询」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which part of the notice answers the media inquiry described in the sample case.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，通知的哪一部分回答了样本案例中的「媒体问询」。

words.enDefinition: The role or activity of connecting journalists with the relevant people or information inside an organisation.

examples.en: The fictional library assigns media liaison to the team that coordinates with reporters and library staff.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆把「媒体联络工作」交给负责协调记者与馆员的团队。

examples.en: Our class distinguishes media liaison from the work of preparing interpretive labels for the fictional exhibition itself.
examples.zh: 全班把「媒体联络工作」与为虚构展览本身编写解说标签的工作区分开。

words.enDefinition: An organised directory of relevant media outlets or contacts, typically maintained for handling media communication.

examples.en: The fictional media contact list contains only public office contacts for local newspapers and the campus radio station.
examples.zh: 虚构的「媒体联络名单」只收录本地报纸和校园电台公开的办公联络信息。

examples.en: Our classroom exercise asks which media contact list was relevant to the fictional library's announcement.
examples.zh: 课堂练习询问，哪份「媒体联络名单」与虚构图书馆的公告相关。

collocations: media contact list for a project

words.enDefinition: A written announcement supplied by an organisation to the media to communicate news or other public information.

examples.en: The fictional museum issues a press release announcing the exhibition dates and the opening hours for visitors.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆发布一篇「公关新闻稿」，宣布展览日期和对访客开放的时段。

examples.en: Our casebook compares the press release with the separate report written by the fictional local newspaper.
examples.zh: 案例教材将「公关新闻稿」与虚构本地报纸另行撰写的报道作比较。

words.enDefinition: The title at the top of an organisation's press release, summarising the main announcement.

examples.en: The press release headline names the fictional gallery's reopening, while the first paragraph gives the date.
examples.zh: 「公关新闻稿标题」提到虚构画廊重新开放，第一段则给出日期。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the press release headline reflects the announcement described in the body text.
examples.zh: 全班核对「公关新闻稿标题」是否对应正文所述的公告内容。

words.enDefinition: The opening paragraph or sentence of a press release that presents its main news or point.

examples.en: The press release lead specifies when the fictional reading room will open and who can use it.
examples.zh: 「公关新闻稿导语」写明虚构阅览室何时开放、哪些人可以使用。

examples.en: Our tutor asks which essential information appears in the press release lead and which comes later.
examples.zh: 老师询问，哪些核心信息出现在「公关新闻稿导语」里，哪些留到后文。

collocations: details in the press release lead

words.zhGloss: 公关新闻稿固定机构简介
words.enDefinition: A reusable section of a press release that provides standard background information about the issuing organisation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 公关新闻稿固定机构简介

examples.en: The fictional gallery includes its mission and founding year in the press release boilerplate below the announcement.
examples.zh: 虚构画廊在公告下方的「公关新闻稿固定机构简介」中列出使命与创立年份。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which details belong in the press release boilerplate rather than in the changing announcement.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，哪些细节应该放进「公关新闻稿固定机构简介」，而不是放进随事件变化的公告内容。

words.zhGloss: 公关新闻稿发稿地点与日期行
words.enDefinition: A line commonly giving the place and date of issue at the beginning of a press release.
acceptedZhAnswers: 公关新闻稿发稿地点与日期行

examples.en: The sample press release dateline gives a fictional city name and the date of the museum announcement.
examples.zh: 样本「公关新闻稿发稿地点与日期行」给出一个虚构城市的名称和博物馆公告的日期。

examples.en: Our worksheet separates the press release dateline from the dates of the exhibition described in the announcement.
examples.zh: 练习单将「公关新闻稿发稿地点与日期行」与公告正文里的展览日期区分开。

collocations: date in a press release dateline
format of a press release dateline

words.enDefinition: A label indicating that the organisation is making an announcement available for publication without a waiting period.

examples.en: The fictional announcement carries the words for immediate release above the headline on the first page.
examples.zh: 虚构公告在第一页标题上方标有「供立即发布」字样。

examples.en: Our casebook asks students to identify what for immediate release means on the fictional exhibition statement.
examples.zh: 案例教材让学生辨认虚构展览声明上的「供立即发布」表示什么。

collocations: mark a statement for immediate release
label a press release for immediate release

words.enDefinition: An arrangement under which participating journalists receive information in advance and agree to hold publication until a stated time.

examples.en: The casebook describes a media embargo on a fictional announcement until the date specified in the sample document.
examples.zh: 案例教材介绍一项虚构公告的「媒体发布延时约定」，持续到样本文书所指的时间。

examples.en: Did reporters in the fictional example agree to the media embargo before receiving the material?
examples.zh: 虚构示例中的记者是否在收到材料之前就同意了「媒体发布延时约定」？

collocations: publication time under a media embargo

words.enDefinition: A short notice giving journalists practical information about a forthcoming event or opportunity to cover it.

examples.en: The fictional press office issues a media advisory listing when and where the exhibition preview will take place.
examples.zh: 虚构新闻联络办公室发出「媒体采访活动预告」，写明展览预览活动的时间和地点。

examples.en: Our class compares the media advisory for the event with the fuller announcement issued afterward in the sample.
examples.zh: 全班对比本场活动的「媒体采访活动预告」与样本中在事后发布的较完整公告。

collocations: event details in a media advisory

words.enDefinition: A collection of materials that an organisation makes available to journalists, such as background information and approved images.

examples.en: The fictional gallery's press kit includes a description of the exhibition and several approved photographs for publication.
examples.zh: 虚构画廊的「媒体资料包」包含展览说明及几张已获准发表的照片。

examples.en: Our seminar identifies which item in the press kit gives reporters general background about the fictional institution.
examples.zh: 研讨课辨认「媒体资料包」中哪件材料向记者介绍虚构机构的一般背景。

collocations: include a fact sheet in a press kit

words.enDefinition: A meeting or session in which an organisation gives journalists information and may answer questions about a particular topic.

examples.en: The fictional university holds a press briefing to explain how the temporary reading room will operate.
examples.zh: 虚构大学举办「媒体情况说明会」，解释临时阅览室将怎样运行。

examples.en: Our exercise distinguishes the press briefing from the short written notice sent before the fictional event.
examples.zh: 练习区分了「媒体情况说明会」和虚构活动开始前发出的简短书面通知。

words.enDefinition: A period or event when a spokesperson or other representative is available to take questions from journalists.

examples.en: The fictional advisory lists a media availability just after the exhibition preview with the university's designated spokesperson.
examples.zh: 虚构预告列出展览预览后紧接的一段「可供媒体采访的时段」，届时大学指定发言人将接受提问。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks how long the media availability lasts according to the schedule for the fictional meeting.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，按照虚构会议的日程，「可供媒体采访的时段」有多长。

words.enDefinition: A session set aside for journalists to ask questions and receive answers from an organisation's representatives.

examples.en: A media Q&A session follows the briefing so reporters can ask about the changed opening hours.
examples.zh: 说明会之后设有「媒体问答环节」，记者可以询问调整后的开放时间。

examples.en: The sample transcript shows how the media Q&A session addressed questions about transport to the venue.
examples.zh: 文字记录样本展示了「媒体问答环节」怎样回应前往会场的交通问题。

collocations: questions during a media Q&A session

words.enDefinition: Words drafted before a person delivers them in a speech, statement, or briefing.

examples.en: The fictional director's prepared remarks describe the project before the media ask about the library's collection.
examples.zh: 虚构总监的「预先准备的发言稿」先介绍项目，随后媒体再问到馆藏。

examples.en: Our exercise compares the prepared remarks with the additional comments in the fictional briefing transcript.
examples.zh: 练习把「预先准备的发言稿」与虚构说明会记录中的补充发言作比较。

words.enDefinition: An official comment or position an organisation provides to journalists on a particular issue or event.

examples.en: The fictional college issues a media statement confirming that its reading room will reopen on Monday.
examples.zh: 虚构大学发出一份「向媒体发布的声明」，确认阅览室将于周一重新开放。

examples.en: Our casebook compares the media statement with the more detailed background material supplied to the fictional reporters.
examples.zh: 案例教材将「向媒体发布的声明」与发给虚构记者的较详细背景材料作比较。

words.enDefinition: An invitation asking members of the press to attend an event or related media opportunity.

examples.en: The fictional gallery sends a press invitation for the morning preview rather than the evening public reception.
examples.zh: 虚构画廊发出的「媒体采访邀请」针对上午预览，而非晚间公众招待会。

examples.en: Our class reads the press invitation to identify which part of the fictional event journalists may attend.
examples.zh: 全班阅读「媒体采访邀请」，找出记者可以参加虚构活动的哪个环节。

words.enDefinition: Formal authorization for eligible journalists and other media staff to cover a specified event or venue.

examples.en: The fictional event guide puts media accreditation in a separate section from registration for the general public.
examples.zh: 虚构活动指南把「媒体采访资格认证」和公众报名分别列在不同章节。

examples.en: Our casebook asks which office handles media accreditation for the fictional exhibition preview described in the advisory.
examples.zh: 案例教材询问，公告所述虚构展览预览的「媒体采访资格认证」由哪个部门处理。

words.enDefinition: Documents or badges that identify a person's press role or show authorisation to cover an event.

examples.en: The fictional event notes say that press credentials identify journalists admitted to the media preview session.
examples.zh: 虚构活动说明写道，「媒体采访证件」用于识别获准参加媒体预览的记者。

examples.en: Our worksheet separates press credentials from the public visitor passes shown in the fictional event guide.
examples.zh: 练习单把「媒体采访证件」与虚构活动指南展示的公众访客通行证分开。

words.enDefinition: A staffed point where registered journalists report on arrival and receive event information or identification.

examples.en: The fictional venue places a media check-in desk near the entrance used for the exhibition preview.
examples.zh: 虚构场地在展览预览活动的入口附近设置「媒体签到处」。

examples.en: Our guide labels the media check-in desk separately from the desk for general visitors at the fictional event.
examples.zh: 指南在虚构活动示意中，把「媒体签到处」与公众访客接待台分别标注。

collocations: report to the media check-in desk
location of the media check-in desk

words.zhGloss: 向媒体提出的报道建议
words.enDefinition: A concise suggestion to a journalist or media outlet that a particular development may warrant coverage.
acceptedZhAnswers: 向媒体提出的报道建议

examples.en: The sample media pitch points a reporter to the fictional museum's schedule and explains the event's local relevance.
examples.zh: 「向媒体提出的报道建议」样本告诉记者虚构博物馆的日程，并解释为什么活动与本地有关。

examples.en: Our seminar identifies which information in the media pitch is independently confirmed by the fictional public announcement.
examples.zh: 研讨课辨认「向媒体提出的报道建议」中哪些信息由虚构的公开公告独立证实。

collocations: relevant details in a media pitch

words.enDefinition: An organised record showing media enquiries, their topics, and the status of responses.

examples.en: The fictional media inquiry log lists which questions about opening hours have received a confirmed response.
examples.zh: 虚构「媒体问询登记表」列出了哪些关于开放时间的问题已经得到经确认的回复。

examples.en: Our class examines the media inquiry log to see whether the fictional press team left any question unanswered.
examples.zh: 全班查看「媒体问询登记表」，判断虚构媒体团队是否仍有哪些问题未答。

collocations: status recorded in a media inquiry log

words.enDefinition: A request from a journalist or outlet to interview a representative, participant, or other relevant person.

examples.en: The fictional press office receives a media interview request about the university's expanded exhibition dates next month.
examples.zh: 虚构新闻联络办公室收到一项关于大学下月延长展期的「媒体采访请求」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which department should receive the media interview request in the fictional organisation chart.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，按照虚构机构图，哪个部门应该接收「媒体采访请求」。

collocations: respond to a media interview request

words.enDefinition: A document providing standard answers to expected questions from journalists about a topic or announcement.

examples.en: The fictional media Q&A document explains when the temporary study room opens and how to find it.
examples.zh: 虚构「媒体问答资料」解释了临时自习室何时开放以及如何找到它。

examples.en: Our class uses the media Q&A document to compare answers prepared for two different fictional opening schedules.
examples.zh: 全班用「媒体问答资料」比较为两个不同虚构开放日程准备的答案。

collocations: questions covered by a media Q&A document

words.zhGloss: 向媒体分发公关新闻稿
words.enDefinition: Making a press release available to relevant media outlets or recipients through an established service or channel.
acceptedZhAnswers: 向媒体分发公关新闻稿

examples.en: The sample plan lists press release distribution as a separate task from editing the announcement's first draft.
examples.zh: 样本计划把「向媒体分发公关新闻稿」和编辑公告初稿分列为两项工作。

examples.en: Our fictional timetable assigns press release distribution to the same office that posts the library's announcements.
examples.zh: 虚构日程把「向媒体分发公关新闻稿」交给同一个负责发布图书馆公告的部门。

words.enDefinition: A collection that preserves past releases and makes them available for reference.

examples.en: The fictional institution's press release archive contains past opening dates announced over several terms of the exhibition.
examples.zh: 虚构机构的「公关新闻稿档案库」保存了几学期展览期间曾公布的开放日期。

examples.en: Our classroom exercise uses the press release archive to locate the first public reference to the project.
examples.zh: 课堂练习用「公关新闻稿档案库」查找有关项目的最早公开提法。

collocations: records in a press release archive

words.zhGloss: 供媒体参考的背景资料
words.enDefinition: A document giving journalists context, history, or explanatory detail about an organisation, project, or issue.
acceptedZhAnswers: 供媒体参考的背景资料

examples.en: The fictional university's media backgrounder explains how the reading programme began and what it currently offers.
examples.zh: 虚构大学的「供媒体参考的背景资料」解释阅读项目如何启动，以及目前提供什么。

examples.en: Our class reads the media backgrounder alongside the shorter announcement about next week's fictional opening event.
examples.zh: 全班将「供媒体参考的背景资料」与关于下周虚构开放活动的较短公告对照阅读。

collocations: include context in a media backgrounder

words.zhGloss: 供媒体使用的事实要览
words.enDefinition: A short reference sheet listing verified details that journalists can consult about an event, service, or organisation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 供媒体使用的事实要览

examples.en: The fictional fact sheet for the media lists the exhibition dates, venue, and number of participating groups.
examples.zh: 虚构「供媒体使用的事实要览」列出展览日期、场地和参与团体数量。

examples.en: Our worksheet checks whether the totals in the fact sheet for the media match the fictional programme records.
examples.zh: 练习单核对「供媒体使用的事实要览」中的总数与虚构项目记录是否一致。

collocations: publish a fact sheet for the media
verify a fact sheet for the media
details in a fact sheet for the media

words.enDefinition: A section appended to some press releases containing background details or practical information for journalists.

examples.en: The fictional press release places notes to editors after the main text and includes background on the organisation.
examples.zh: 虚构公关新闻稿把「致编辑附注」放在正文之后，并附上机构背景。

examples.en: Our class identifies which paragraph belongs under notes to editors for the fictional community exhibition announcement.
examples.zh: 全班辨认，虚构社区展览公告中的哪一段属于「致编辑附注」。

collocations: details in the notes to editors

words.enDefinition: A statement delivered by a person in front of a camera for a media recording or broadcast.

examples.en: The fictional director gives an on-camera statement before the media ask questions about the new reading room.
examples.zh: 虚构总监在媒体就新阅览室提问之前发表了一份「面对镜头发表的声明」。

examples.en: Our class compares the on-camera statement with the written notice released by the fictional university that morning.
examples.zh: 全班将「面对镜头发表的声明」与虚构大学当日上午发布的书面通知作比较。

words.enDefinition: An organisation's published contact information for journalists seeking details or official comment.

examples.en: The fictional notice places media contact details at the end for journalists requiring clarification about exhibition dates.
examples.zh: 虚构通知末尾提供「媒体联络信息」，供需要进一步确认展期的记者使用。

examples.en: Our exercise distinguishes media contact details from the address where visitors can ask about the fictional event.
examples.zh: 练习区分「媒体联络信息」和访客咨询虚构活动时可使用的地址。

collocations: media contact details on a press release

words.enDefinition: An official statement that an organisation or representative makes directly available to the public.

examples.en: The fictional library posts a public statement confirming that a temporary reading room is available this week.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆发布一份「公开声明」，确认本周可以使用一处临时阅览室。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares the public statement with a separate discussion intended only for the fictional organising committee.
examples.zh: 练习单比较「公开声明」与只面向虚构组织委员会的另一项内部讨论。

words.enDefinition: A communication informing a local or affected community about recent changes, progress, or decisions.

examples.en: The fictional museum issues a community update about the revised schedule for its weekend reading programme.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆发布一份「面向社区的最新通报」，介绍周末阅读项目调整后的时段。

examples.en: Our class examines whether the community update addresses questions raised by residents in the fictional listening session.
examples.zh: 全班看「面向社区的最新通报」是否回应了居民在虚构意见听取会上提出的问题。

words.enDefinition: A public notice explaining a temporary interruption or change to a service and, where known, its expected scope.

examples.en: The fictional college posts a service disruption notice after the main study room becomes temporarily unavailable.
examples.zh: 主要自习室暂时无法使用后，虚构大学张贴了「服务中断通知」。

examples.en: Our worksheet checks which temporary arrangements are described in the service disruption notice for the fictional library.
examples.zh: 练习单核对虚构图书馆的「服务中断通知」说明了哪些临时安排。

collocations: details in a service disruption notice

words.enDefinition: The involvement of members of the public through activities such as discussion, consultation, or contribution to a project.

examples.en: The casebook uses public engagement to describe the fictional library's opportunities for residents to contribute ideas.
examples.zh: 案例教材用「公众参与」来描述虚构图书馆让居民提供想法的机会。

examples.en: Our seminar discusses public engagement after reviewing the participation summary for the fictional university's exhibition project.
examples.zh: 研讨课阅读虚构大学展览项目的参与情况摘要后，讨论了「公众参与」。

words.enDefinition: A process in which an organisation or public body invites public views on a proposal or decision under consideration.

examples.en: The fictional council begins a public consultation on proposed changes to the local reading room's weekend hours.
examples.zh: 虚构地方议会就调整本地阅览室周末时段的提议启动「公开征询意见」。

examples.en: Our class asks which options were still open for discussion during the public consultation in the sample timeline.
examples.zh: 全班询问，在样本时间线里的「公开征询意见」期间，哪些选项仍供讨论。

words.enDefinition: A session giving members of a community information and context about a local issue, activity, or decision.

examples.en: At the community briefing, a representative explained how the fictional garden would reopen after the pathways were repaired.
examples.zh: 在「社区情况说明会」上，一名代表解释了虚构花园将在路径维修后怎样重新开放。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which community briefing in the fictional schedule is intended for neighbouring residents this week.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构日程里哪场「社区情况说明会」本周面向附近居民。

words.enDefinition: An organised session mainly intended to hear members of the public describe concerns, views, or experiences.

examples.en: At the fictional public listening session, residents describe what they need from a temporary reading facility.
examples.zh: 在虚构「公众意见听取会」上，居民说出他们对临时阅读设施的需求。

examples.en: Our class reads the public listening session summary before considering how the fictional committee responded to common concerns.
examples.zh: 全班阅读「公众意见听取会」摘要，然后考虑虚构委员会如何回应常见关切。

collocations: feedback from a public listening session

words.enDefinition: A concise account of the main views and themes raised during a consultation.

examples.en: The fictional consultation summary records several views about extending opening hours and explains how responses were grouped.
examples.zh: 虚构「意见征询摘要」记录了几种关于延长开放时间的意见，并解释答复如何分类。

examples.en: Our worksheet identifies which concerns in the consultation summary are mentioned again in the fictional decision document.
examples.zh: 练习单辨认「意见征询摘要」中哪些关切再次出现在虚构决定文件中。

words.zhGloss: 对公众意见征询的正式回应
words.enDefinition: An organisation's public account of how it considered feedback from a consultation and what it proposes to do next.
acceptedZhAnswers: 对公众意见征询的正式回应

examples.en: The fictional university's response to public consultation explains why one option changed after comments from library users.
examples.zh: 虚构大学的「对公众意见征询的正式回应」解释，为什么收到图书馆使用者意见后修改了一项选项。

examples.en: Our class compares the response to public consultation with the document that originally invited feedback in the exercise.
examples.zh: 全班将「对公众意见征询的正式回应」与练习中最初征询意见的文件作比较。

collocations: publish a response to public consultation
draft a response to public consultation
decision explained in a response to public consultation

words.zhGloss: 面向公众的常见问题解答
words.enDefinition: A set of published answers to common questions intended for people outside the organisation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 面向公众的常见问题解答

examples.en: The fictional library publishes a public-facing FAQ about temporary opening hours alongside its longer notice to visitors.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆在较长的访客通知旁，发布一份关于临时开放时间的「面向公众的常见问题解答」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether the public-facing FAQ explains how readers can reach the replacement study space easily.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，「面向公众的常见问题解答」是否说明读者如何方便地到达替代自习空间。

words.enDefinition: Public information provided in formats and language that people with differing access needs can use.

examples.en: The fictional venue offers accessible public information about the new entrance in formats visitors can use independently.
examples.zh: 虚构场馆以访客可独立使用的形式，提供关于新入口的「无障碍公众信息」。

examples.en: Our class examines whether the accessible public information includes the same practical details as the original notice.
examples.zh: 全班查看「无障碍公众信息」是否包含原通知中的同样实用细节。

words.enDefinition: A notice made available in a different format to suit particular access or communication needs.

examples.en: The fictional library offers an alternative-format notice containing the same opening information as the printed version.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆提供「替代格式通知」，其中的开放信息与印刷版相同。

examples.en: Our exercise checks that the alternative-format notice reflects the revised dates shown in the standard notice too.
examples.zh: 练习核查「替代格式通知」也体现了标准通知所列的调整后日期。

words.enDefinition: Communication during and around a serious disruption, intended to inform affected people and explain the organisation's response.

examples.en: The seminar introduces crisis communication with a fictional university maintaining public updates during an extended venue closure.
examples.zh: 研讨课借虚构大学在场地长期关闭期间持续向公众通报的例子，介绍「危机沟通」。

examples.en: Our casebook discusses crisis communication by comparing what was confirmed in the first and later fictional statements.
examples.zh: 案例教材对照第一份和后续虚构声明中已经确认的内容，讨论「危机沟通」。

words.enDefinition: A plan assigning communication roles, information checks, and arrangements for reaching affected groups during a serious disruption.

examples.en: The fictional crisis communication plan specifies who will confirm the facts before issuing a notice about venue availability.
examples.zh: 虚构「危机沟通预案」规定，发布场地能否使用的通知之前，由谁确认事实。

examples.en: Our classroom exercise asks whether the crisis communication plan identifies how affected readers would receive the updates.
examples.zh: 课堂练习询问，「危机沟通预案」是否说明受影响的读者将怎样收到后续通报。

words.enDefinition: The group assigned to coordinate reliable communication with affected people and the media during a serious disruption.

examples.en: The fictional crisis communications team includes staff who can verify programme dates before publishing public updates.
examples.zh: 虚构「危机沟通团队」的成员中，有人可以在发布公众通报前核实项目日期。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks how the crisis communications team worked with the office responsible for the venue's reopening.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，「危机沟通团队」怎样与负责场地重新开放的部门合作。

collocations: responsibilities of a crisis communications team

words.enDefinition: A statement prepared or issued in response to an external question or a new development.

examples.en: The fictional press office issues a reactive statement after a journalist asks about the missing exhibition dates.
examples.zh: 在记者询问未列明的展出日期后，虚构新闻联络办公室发出一份「应询声明」。

examples.en: Our case compares the reactive statement with an announcement the fictional gallery already planned to publish later.
examples.zh: 案例把「应询声明」与虚构画廊已计划稍后公布的公告作比较。

words.enDefinition: An initial statement that acknowledges an issue and shares verified information while a fuller response is being prepared.

examples.en: The fictional university publishes a holding statement confirming the venue closure while staff check the replacement arrangements.
examples.zh: 虚构大学发布一份「临时回应声明」，确认场地关闭，同时工作人员核实替代安排。

examples.en: Our class discusses which confirmed details appear in the holding statement and which were added in later updates.
examples.zh: 全班讨论哪些已确认细节出现在「临时回应声明」中，哪些在后续通报中添加。

collocations: confirmed details in a holding statement

words.enDefinition: The first status update about an incident, describing what is known at that point and its immediate public implications.

examples.en: The initial incident update confirms that the fictional library entrance remains closed while another route is available.
examples.zh: 「事件初次情况通报」确认虚构图书馆入口仍然关闭，同时还有另一条路线可通行。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which information appeared in the initial incident update and which was added that afternoon.
examples.zh: 练习单询问哪些信息出现在「事件初次情况通报」中，哪些是当天下午加上的。

collocations: facts in an initial incident update

words.enDefinition: Details that have been checked and established as reliable for the purposes of a communication.

examples.en: The fictional museum's update separates confirmed information about opening hours from details still awaiting confirmation that morning.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆上午发布的通报把关于开放时间的「已确认的信息」与尚待确认的细节分开。

examples.en: Our exercise asks which parts of the public statement are confirmed information according to the fictional records.
examples.zh: 练习询问，根据虚构记录，公开声明的哪些部分属于「已确认的信息」。

words.enDefinition: To tell an audience which aspects of an issue or its timing are still uncertain and what that uncertainty means.

examples.en: The press team can communicate uncertainty about the reopening date while giving confirmed details about temporary access.
examples.zh: 媒体团队可以在提供临时通行的已确认细节时，对重新开放日期「说明不确定性」。

examples.en: Our review asks how the institution can communicate uncertainty about a schedule that is still under discussion.
examples.zh: 复核讨论该机构怎样对仍在研究的日程「说明不确定性」。

words.enDefinition: A timetable indicating when an organisation expects to publish new information for the public.

examples.en: The fictional library posts a public update schedule beside its notices about the temporary change to reading rooms.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆在临时更换阅览室的通知旁公布「公众通报时间表」。

examples.en: Our casebook asks whether the public update schedule was easy to find in the fictional public announcements.
examples.zh: 案例教材询问，在虚构公众公告中，是否很容易找到「公众通报时间表」。

words.enDefinition: The next update listed for a stated time or place in a communication schedule.

examples.en: The fictional venue notice gives the time of the next scheduled update about its temporary opening hours.
examples.zh: 虚构场馆通知给出关于临时开放时段的「下一次计划通报」时间。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the next scheduled update actually appeared as promised in the fictional timeline here.
examples.zh: 全班核查，在这条虚构时间线上，「下一次计划通报」是否确实如约发布。

collocations: time of the next scheduled update
wait for the next scheduled update

words.enDefinition: A chronological account of key events and communications connected with an incident.

examples.en: The fictional incident timeline places the first service notice before the later announcement about the replacement room.
examples.zh: 虚构「事件时间线」把第一份服务通知放在后来关于替代房间的公告之前。

examples.en: Our review uses the incident timeline to see when the public first received each piece of information.
examples.zh: 复核用「事件时间线」查看公众首次收到每条信息的时间。

words.enDefinition: A statement explaining the meaning or scope of earlier communication to resolve ambiguity or possible misunderstanding.

examples.en: The fictional library publishes a clarification statement specifying which groups can reserve the temporary reading room.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆发布一份「澄清声明」，说明哪些团体可以预约临时阅览室。

examples.en: Our worksheet checks whether the clarification statement addresses the misunderstanding described in the sample feedback summary.
examples.zh: 练习单核对「澄清声明」是否回应了样本反馈摘要描述的误解。

words.enDefinition: A public notice in which an organization identifies an error in its own earlier communication and supplies the correct information.

examples.en: The fictional university posts a correction notice after its earlier announcement listed the wrong exhibition closing date.
examples.zh: 先前公告写错展览结束日期后，虚构大学发布了「更正通知」。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the correction notice identifies both the original error and the correct replacement date.
examples.zh: 全班核对「更正通知」是否同时指明原错误和替换后的正确日期。

words.enDefinition: A revised version of a previously issued release that fixes an error in its content.

examples.en: The fictional press office labels the corrected press release so readers can identify the version with accurate dates.
examples.zh: 虚构新闻联络办公室标注「更正后的公关新闻稿」，让读者能找到日期准确的版本。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares the corrected press release with the archived original to identify which information was changed.
examples.zh: 练习单比较「更正后的公关新闻稿」和存档原稿，找出哪些信息发生变动。

collocations: date of a corrected press release

words.enDefinition: A record identifying errors that were corrected and showing what was changed and when.

examples.en: The museum's correction log lists the date when staff fixed an incorrect opening time in a public notice.
examples.zh: 博物馆的「公开信息更正记录」列出了工作人员修正公告中错误开放时间的日期。

examples.en: Our class consults the correction log to see when the notice began showing the revised closing date.
examples.zh: 全班查阅「公开信息更正记录」，查看通知从什么时候开始显示调整后的结束日期。

collocations: add an entry to a correction log
date recorded in a correction log

words.enDefinition: A later statement giving additional information or clarification about a matter an organisation has already addressed.

examples.en: The fictional venue's follow-up statement gives confirmed reopening details that were unavailable when the first update appeared.
examples.zh: 虚构场馆的「后续声明」列出首次通报时尚未掌握的、已经确认的重新开放详情。

examples.en: Our class compares the follow-up statement with the earlier notice to identify newly available details about the service.
examples.zh: 全班把「后续声明」与早先的通知作对照，找出后来得到的服务详情。

words.enDefinition: A public explanation of an organisation's responsibility for an issue and the steps it commits to take.

examples.en: The fictional museum's accountability statement explains which office was responsible for approving the mistaken opening time notice.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆的「责任说明」解释了哪个部门负责审批开放时间有误的通知。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares the accountability statement with the later progress report on the fictional organisation's promised changes.
examples.zh: 练习单比较「责任说明」与之后有关虚构机构承诺改进事项的进展报告。

words.enDefinition: An agreed procedure for receiving, verifying, approving, and responding to questions from news media.

examples.en: The fictional media response protocol identifies which office confirms dates before a spokesperson answers press questions publicly.
examples.zh: 虚构「媒体回应规程」规定，发言人公开回答新闻提问之前，由哪个部门确认日期。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the media response protocol identifies a person responsible for correcting a published mistake.
examples.zh: 全班核对「媒体回应规程」是否指明由谁负责纠正已经公布的错误。

collocations: responsibilities under a media response protocol

words.enDefinition: Communication giving verified information to correct an unconfirmed claim circulating among the public or within a group.

examples.en: The fictional library's rumour correction confirms that the temporary reading room remains open on its usual days.
examples.zh: 虚构图书馆的「传言纠正」确认，临时阅览室仍按通常日期开放。

examples.en: Our exercise checks whether the rumour correction cites the confirmed schedule for the fictional public reading programme.
examples.zh: 练习核对「传言纠正」是否引用了虚构公共阅读项目已经确认的日程。

collocations: verified information in a rumour correction

words.enDefinition: A notice describing when or to what extent an interrupted service has become available again.

examples.en: The fictional museum issues a service restoration update confirming that the public reading room has reopened today.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆发布一则「服务恢复通报」，确认公共阅览室今天已重新开放。

examples.en: Our class compares the service restoration update with the earlier notice listing temporary alternatives at the library.
examples.zh: 全班把「服务恢复通报」与此前列明图书馆临时替代方案的通知作比较。

collocations: timing in a service restoration update

words.enDefinition: A rehearsal that tests how a team would communicate in a hypothetical disruption or emergency.

examples.en: The fictional university runs a crisis communications exercise based on a prolonged closure of a campus reading room.
examples.zh: 虚构大学开展一场以校园阅览室长时间关闭为背景的「危机沟通演练」。

examples.en: Our worksheet lists the facts available at the start of the crisis communications exercise for participants to review.
examples.zh: 练习单列出「危机沟通演练」开始时可获得的事实，供参与者阅读。

collocations: findings from a crisis communications exercise

words.enDefinition: An assessment after an incident of how communication worked and which practices could be improved.

examples.en: The post-incident communications review compares when fictional updates were published with when residents reported receiving the information.
examples.zh: 「事件后沟通复盘」将虚构通报的发布时间与居民报告收到信息的时间作比较。

examples.en: Our class asks which communication lessons are supported by the evidence listed in the post-incident communications review.
examples.zh: 全班询问，「事件后沟通复盘」所列证据支持哪些沟通方面的经验教训。

collocations: findings of a post-incident communications review
recommendations from a post-incident communications review

words.enDefinition: Principles and professional standards guiding honest, responsible, and transparent public relations practice.

examples.en: The seminar introduces PR ethics by asking what a fictional organisation should disclose about a funded exhibition.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论虚构机构应公开一场受资助展览的哪些信息，以介绍「公共关系职业伦理」。

examples.en: Our casebook connects PR ethics with correcting an error in a public notice once it is discovered.
examples.zh: 案例教材把「公共关系职业伦理」与发现公众通知有误后作出更正联系起来。

words.enDefinition: The practice of presenting facts correctly and keeping descriptions consistent with the evidence available.

examples.en: The fictional museum checks accuracy in public communication by comparing its notice with the confirmed exhibition schedule.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆将通知与确认的展览日程作比较，检查「公众沟通的准确性」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks how an outdated date affected accuracy in public communication in the fictional case.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，在虚构案例中，过时的日期如何影响「公众沟通的准确性」。

collocations: standards for accuracy in public communication

words.enDefinition: In public relations ethics, the principle of protecting the exchange of accurate and truthful information needed for informed judgement.

examples.en: The PR ethics seminar links the free flow of information to making the fictional institution's correction publicly available.
examples.zh: 公关伦理研讨课把「信息自由流通」与公开虚构机构作出的更正联系起来。

examples.en: Our casebook discusses the free flow of information when readers need timely details about a changed library schedule.
examples.zh: 案例教材讨论读者需要及时了解图书馆日程变动时的「信息自由流通」。

collocations: protect the free flow of information
support the free flow of information
principle of the free flow of information

words.zhGloss: 公关业务中的委托方披露
words.enDefinition: Identifying the client on whose behalf a public relations activity or communication is carried out.
acceptedZhAnswers: 公关业务中的委托方披露

examples.en: The fictional notice illustrates client disclosure in PR by naming the institution that commissioned the communication work.
examples.zh: 虚构通知通过列出委托传播工作的机构，说明「公关业务中的委托方披露」。

examples.en: Our casebook asks where readers can find client disclosure in PR materials prepared for the fictional exhibition.
examples.zh: 案例教材询问，读者可在为虚构展览编写的材料中哪里找到「公关业务中的委托方披露」。

collocations: transparency through client disclosure in PR
example of client disclosure in PR

words.enDefinition: A statement making visible the fact that an organisation or activity receives support from an identified sponsor.

examples.en: The fictional exhibition's sponsorship disclosure names the organisation that contributed funding for the printed programme.
examples.zh: 虚构展览的「赞助关系披露」写明为印制日程册提供资金的机构。

examples.en: Our class asks whether the sponsorship disclosure is easy to locate in the fictional museum's public announcement.
examples.zh: 全班询问，在虚构博物馆的公开公告中是否能轻松找到「赞助关系披露」。

words.zhGloss: 不偏袒政党的公众沟通
words.enDefinition: Public information provided without promoting a political party or taking a party-political position.
acceptedZhAnswers: 不偏袒政党的公众沟通

examples.en: The public service course presents nonpartisan public communication through a fictional notice explaining changes to library services.
examples.zh: 公共服务课程借一份解释图书馆服务变动的虚构通知，介绍「不偏袒政党的公众沟通」。

examples.en: Our class checks that nonpartisan public communication in the example addresses all users of the public service.
examples.zh: 全班核对示例中「不偏袒政党的公众沟通」是否面向公共服务的所有使用者。

words.enDefinition: Communication intended to serve public needs or help people understand matters of shared concern.

examples.en: The seminar illustrates public-interest communication with a fictional programme explaining access to a community reading room.
examples.zh: 研讨课以说明如何使用社区阅览室的虚构项目为例，说明「公共利益传播」。

examples.en: Our casebook asks how public-interest communication in the example addresses residents' practical questions about the changed hours.
examples.zh: 案例教材询问，示例中「公共利益传播」怎样回应居民关于时段变动的实际问题。

words.enDefinition: A systematic assessment of what a communication effort achieved, compared with its goals and relevant evidence.

examples.en: The fictional communications evaluation compares how many people received the notice with whether they understood its contents.
examples.zh: 虚构的「传播评估」将收到通知的人数与这些人是否理解通知内容作比较。

examples.en: A fictional recycling project uses communications evaluation to compare residents' understanding before and after publishing new signs.
examples.zh: 一个虚构的回收项目通过「传播评估」，比较公布新标志前后居民的理解程度。

words.enDefinition: The collection or calculation of indicators showing communication activities, audience responses, or later effects.

examples.en: The textbook introduces communications measurement through a fictional report using several indicators for a university information campaign.
examples.zh: 教材用一份采用多项指标衡量大学信息传播活动的虚构报告，介绍「传播成效测量」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which data sources support communications measurement for each stage of the fictional project.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，哪些数据来源支持虚构项目各阶段的「传播成效测量」。

words.enDefinition: A resource, budget, staff contribution, or other starting input used to plan and carry out communication work.

examples.en: The fictional planning table describes staff time as a communications input for the weekend library information campaign.
examples.zh: 虚构计划表把人员工时列为周末图书馆信息传播活动的一项「传播投入」。

examples.en: Our class distinguishes a communications input listed before the campaign from the materials it produced later.
examples.zh: 全班将传播活动前列出的一项「传播投入」与后来产出的材料区分开。

words.enDefinition: A planned piece of work carried out as part of a project to produce communication materials or experiences.

examples.en: The fictional plan records a public briefing as a communications activity for the residents' library access project.
examples.zh: 虚构计划把一场公众说明会记作居民图书馆使用项目的一项「传播活动事项」。

examples.en: Our class asks which communications activity took place before the first public update appeared in the fictional timeline.
examples.zh: 全班询问，虚构时间线上第一份公众通报发布前开展了哪项「传播活动事项」。

words.enDefinition: Material, coverage, or other immediate result produced or delivered through communication activity.

examples.en: The evaluation table lists the published library notice as a communications output from the fictional project.
examples.zh: 评估表把已发布的图书馆通知列为虚构项目的一项「传播产出」。

examples.en: Our class compares a communications output with evidence of what readers understood after receiving the fictional notice.
examples.zh: 全班将一项「传播产出」与读者收到虚构通知后理解了什么的证据作比较。

words.enDefinition: An immediate audience response to communication, such as attention, understanding, or what the audience takes from it.

examples.en: The evaluation measures a communications outtake by asking whether readers understood which library entrance remained open.
examples.zh: 评估通过询问读者是否知道图书馆哪个入口仍然开放，测量一项「受众即时反应」。

examples.en: Our worksheet places a communications outtake after message delivery and before longer changes in the fictional timeline.
examples.zh: 练习单在虚构时间线中，把「受众即时反应」放在消息传达之后、较长期的变化之前。

collocations: audience understanding as a communications outtake

words.enDefinition: A change in knowledge, attitudes, trust, intentions, or behaviour linked to communication and assessed in relation to its objectives.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation reports a communications outcome when more readers use the correct entrance after receiving the update.
examples.zh: 发布通报后更多读者使用正确入口，虚构评估把这一变化列为一项「传播结果」。

examples.en: Our class asks what evidence connects the observed communications outcome to the fictional campaign rather than unrelated events.
examples.zh: 全班询问，哪些证据把观察到的「传播结果」与虚构传播活动相联系，而非归于无关事件。

words.enDefinition: A broader or longer-term effect on an organisation, its stakeholders, or society to which communication contributes.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation discusses communications impact by examining whether residents found library services easier to access over time.
examples.zh: 虚构评估考察居民是否逐渐觉得图书馆服务更容易使用，从而讨论「传播影响」。

examples.en: Our seminar asks which evidence supports a claim about communications impact in the fictional public service report.
examples.zh: 研讨课询问，什么证据支持虚构公共服务报告中有关「传播影响」的说法。

words.enDefinition: An initial measure or description of conditions before a communication activity, used as a reference for later evaluation.

examples.en: The fictional report uses a communications baseline showing how many readers understood the opening hours before the campaign.
examples.zh: 虚构报告采用一项「传播评估基线」，显示传播活动开始前有多少读者理解开放时间。

examples.en: Our class checks the communications baseline before comparing later survey results in the sample evaluation table.
examples.zh: 全班先查看「传播评估基线」，再比较对照评估表中的后续调查结果。

words.enDefinition: A structured approach connecting public relations objectives with indicators of activities, responses, and relevant effects.

examples.en: The fictional museum's PR measurement framework links published notices to separate measures of understanding among the intended audiences.
examples.zh: 虚构博物馆的「公关测量框架」将发布的通知与面向预定受众的理解程度指标相联系。

examples.en: Our exercise uses a PR measurement framework to distinguish audience response from the number of notices published.
examples.zh: 练习用「公关测量框架」区分受众反应与发布通知的数量。

collocations: indicators in a PR measurement framework

words.enDefinition: The International Association for Measurement and Evaluation of Communication's framework linking objectives, inputs, activities, and resulting effects.

examples.en: The seminar uses the AMEC Integrated Evaluation Framework to organise evidence for a fictional public information project.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「AMEC整合评估框架」整理一项虚构公众信息项目的证据。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares two categories from the AMEC Integrated Evaluation Framework in a fictional communication evaluation exercise.
examples.zh: 练习单在虚构的传播评估练习中，比较「AMEC整合评估框架」里的两个类别。

collocations: use the AMEC Integrated Evaluation Framework
stages of the AMEC Integrated Evaluation Framework
indicators in the AMEC Integrated Evaluation Framework

words.enDefinition: AMEC's principles for setting goals and assessing communication work through transparent measurement of relevant results and impact.

examples.en: The course introduces the Barcelona Principles before asking students to evaluate a fictional university communication report.
examples.zh: 课程先介绍「巴塞罗那原则」，再请学生评估一份虚构大学传播报告。

examples.en: The reading on the Barcelona Principles explains why an advertising cost estimate is unsuitable as a value measure.
examples.zh: 有关「巴塞罗那原则」的读物解释了，用估算的广告费用衡量传播价值为什么不合适。

collocations: evaluation guided by the Barcelona Principles

words.enDefinition: The systematic review of publicly available media to identify relevant coverage or mentions.

examples.en: The classroom exercise uses media monitoring to identify published articles about a fictional community reading project.
examples.zh: 课堂练习用「媒体监测」找出已经发表、涉及一项虚构社区阅读项目的文章。

examples.en: Our report describes the sources included in media monitoring for the fictional university's communication evaluation.
examples.zh: 报告说明，对虚构大学开展传播评估时，「媒体监测」涵盖了哪些来源。

words.enDefinition: An examination of coverage to understand what was reported, how it was presented, and which themes were prominent.

examples.en: The fictional coverage analysis compares how different local outlets described the university's changes to its reading services.
examples.zh: 虚构「媒体报道分析」比较不同地方媒体如何描述大学对阅读服务的调整。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the coverage analysis explains which public statements were quoted in the fictional articles.
examples.zh: 全班核对「媒体报道分析」是否说明虚构文章引用了哪些公开声明。

words.enDefinition: The count of relevant media items in a specified set of outlets or reporting period.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation compares coverage volume before and after the launch of a weekend community reading programme.
examples.zh: 虚构评估比较周末社区阅读项目推出前后的「报道数量」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether duplicated articles are included in coverage volume for the fictional reporting period in question.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构报告期的「报道数量」是否纳入重复发表的文章。

words.enDefinition: An occurrence in which published media refer to an organisation, person, project, or topic.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation records one media mention when the local paper names the exhibition in a calendar listing.
examples.zh: 虚构评估记录了一次「媒体提及」，因为地方报纸在日程条目中提到了展览名称。

examples.en: Our class checks whether each media mention refers to the same fictional programme or to a different event.
examples.zh: 全班核对各次「媒体提及」说的是同一虚构项目，还是其他活动。

words.enDefinition: A saved copy or extract of a published media item kept for reference or evaluation.

examples.en: The fictional report includes a media clipping from the local paper describing the library's temporary reading room.
examples.zh: 虚构报告收录一篇「媒体报道摘录」，内容是地方报纸对图书馆临时阅览室的描述。

examples.en: Our class reads the media clipping alongside the original statement to check which points were quoted.
examples.zh: 全班将「媒体报道摘录」与原声明对照阅读，核查引用了哪些要点。

words.enDefinition: A report collecting or summarising relevant coverage for a specified topic, organisation, or time period.

examples.en: The fictional media coverage report lists the original articles and summarises how frequently the exhibition was mentioned.
examples.zh: 虚构「媒体报道汇总报告」列出原文，并概括展览被提及的频次。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the media coverage report identifies the time period and outlets included in the sample.
examples.zh: 全班核对「媒体报道汇总报告」是否写明样本涵盖的时段与媒体。

collocations: reporting period in a media coverage report

words.enDefinition: How noticeable a topic or organisation is within coverage, such as whether it appears in the headline or only briefly.

examples.en: The fictional report assesses coverage prominence by distinguishing headline references from brief mentions in the body text.
examples.zh: 虚构报告区分标题提及与正文中的简短提及，以评估「报道中的显著程度」。

examples.en: Our class compares coverage prominence across two fictional articles that discuss the same university reading programme.
examples.zh: 全班比较两篇讨论同一大学阅读项目的虚构文章中的「报道中的显著程度」。

words.enDefinition: A qualitative assessment of how media coverage presents a subject, such as favourably, neutrally, or critically.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation considers coverage tone separately from the number of articles mentioning the campus exhibition.
examples.zh: 虚构评估分别考虑「媒体报道的语气倾向」和提及校园展览的文章数量。

examples.en: Our class discusses coverage tone after comparing two fictional reports that describe the same event differently.
examples.zh: 全班对照两份以不同方式描述同一活动的虚构报道，然后讨论「媒体报道的语气倾向」。

words.zhGloss: 媒体报道对核心信息的体现
words.enDefinition: The extent to which designated key messages are reflected in independent coverage or other analysed content.
acceptedZhAnswers: 媒体报道对核心信息的体现

examples.en: The fictional evaluation examines message pull-through by checking whether local coverage included the central point about public access.
examples.zh: 虚构评估核对当地报道是否包含公众使用权限这一核心要点，以分析「媒体报道对核心信息的体现」。

examples.en: Our class distinguishes message pull-through from simply counting how many articles mention the fictional institution by name.
examples.zh: 全班把「媒体报道对核心信息的体现」与仅统计多少篇文章提到虚构机构名称的做法区分开。

words.enDefinition: An estimate of the audience that might have encountered coverage, based on source audience figures or other stated assumptions.

examples.en: The fictional report labels potential reach of coverage as an estimate based on readership figures for the outlets.
examples.zh: 虚构报告将「报道的潜在触达人数」标注为根据相关媒体读者量得出的估计。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares potential reach of coverage with direct evidence about what fictional readers actually saw.
examples.zh: 练习单将「报道的潜在触达人数」与有关虚构读者实际看到哪些内容的直接证据进行比较。

collocations: assumptions behind potential reach of coverage

words.enDefinition: Use, republication, or coverage by media outlets following the release of material from an organisation.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation records media pickup after two local outlets use information from the community centre's announcement.
examples.zh: 两家当地媒体采用社区中心公告中的信息后，虚构评估记录了「媒体采用公关材料」的情况。

examples.en: Our example compares media pickup across outlets and notes which ones added independent reporting to the announcement.
examples.zh: 示例比较不同媒体「媒体采用公关材料」的情况，并指出哪些媒体在公告信息之外作了独立采访。

collocations: media pickup of a press release

words.enDefinition: The confidence that affected or interested groups have in an organisation's reliability, honesty, or conduct.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation measures stakeholder trust after the museum publishes several timely corrections to its notices.
examples.zh: 博物馆及时更正几则通知后，虚构评估衡量了「利益相关方信任」。

examples.en: The report treats stakeholder trust as an intermediate outcome before examining longer-term changes in community participation.
examples.zh: 报告将「利益相关方信任」视为中期结果，然后考察社区参与较长期的变化。

words.enDefinition: A reference value or standard used to compare the performance of a communication effort with another effort or period.

examples.en: The fictional evaluation uses a communications benchmark drawn from a similar campaign to compare notice publication times.
examples.zh: 虚构评估采用一项来自类似活动的「传播比较基准」，用来比较通知发布时间。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the communications benchmark comes from a comparable kind of public information campaign.
examples.zh: 全班核对「传播比较基准」是否来自可比较的公众信息传播活动。

words.enDefinition: A disfavoured method estimating the price of buying advertising space or time comparable to earned media coverage.

examples.en: The AMEC reading discusses advertising value equivalency as an unsuitable way to measure the value of public communication.
examples.zh: AMEC 读物指出，「广告价值等值估算」不适于衡量公众沟通的价值。

examples.en: Our class compares advertising value equivalency with evidence of audience understanding in the fictional evaluation report.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构评估报告中的「广告价值等值估算」和有关受众理解程度的证据。
